expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014..TKT-016, intro + non-goals in the header), cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-012; CLI-001 and CLI-006 amended) and event-log.md (LOG-001 amended). Final message: 'I amended the repo's existing specs instead of adding a new file, because the repo keeps ticket rules in tickets.md and the command surface in cli.md.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'A ticket that is not closed after its due time is overdue, see TKT-014. Overdue is not a fourth state...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. Non-goals: 'These are out of scope for overdue tickets:' with 5 boundaries (no escalation/notification, no due-time change, no business hours, no pause/snooze, no late-close record). Note the purpose sentence 'Overdue tickets let support agents see which tickets passed their due time.' is glued onto the non-goals lead line.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012 (check_run's 9 items in event-log.md are all pre-existing; LOG-001 was amended, not added). Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. CLI-010 and CLI-011 each have 5 sentences plus an example and a TODO; longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '`OVERDUE` in place of the state' with example. Filter: CLI-011 'Tickets that are not overdue are not printed.' Order: TKT-016 'The ticket with the earliest due time comes first... ID ascending' with a CLI-011 example. Exact due: TKT-014 'At exactly its due time a ticket is not yet overdue' + example 13:00 vs 13:00:01. Closed: TKT-014 'never overdue' + TODO. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; questions.md Q6 also lists 'Empty output' as a non-blocking assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). Outcomes are CLI lines, stdout and exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is not a fourth state. It is a fact about the ticket at the time a command runs. The log holds no event for it.' TKT-015: 'No event is appended when a ticket becomes overdue.' LOG-001 amended: 'That holds for `list` and for `overdue`.' and flagged as a contract change in questions.md. INV-001/INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014: 'The due time is the one from TKT-005.' CLI-010 states explicitly: 'The order of the lines stays as TKT-013 sets it.'
